items.title: 2026-018: Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP
items.summary: CERT-EU advisory: two critical PHP flaws allowing unauthenticated remote code execution are fixed in 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. PoCs are circulating, raising exploitation likelihood.

items.title: 2026-019: Critical Vulnerability in GitLab Community and Enterprise Editions
items.summary: CERT-EU warns of a critical GitLab CE/EE flaw enabling unauthenticated arbitrary code execution on the server; patch internet-facing instances first and assess for compromise.

items.title: 2026-017: Critical Vulnerability in Cisco Secure Email Gateway
items.summary: A critical flaw in the AMP feature of Cisco Secure Email Gateway allows unauthenticated remote attackers to write files and run commands as root; Cisco PSIRT confirms active exploitation.

items.title: AI coding agents hijacked using AGENTS.md file in Downloads folder
items.summary: Researchers found a malicious AGENTS.md instruction file in a user's Downloads folder that hijacked an AI coding agent into installing a rogue npm package, a prompt-injection style supply chain risk.

items.title: Forgotten AI agents may still access sensitive company data
items.summary: Arrakis Security reports 76% of enabled AI agents had not run in 60 days yet retained credentials and system connections, creating dormant but privileged access paths.

items.title: Japanese companies compensate users as cyberattacks buffet economy
items.summary: Reuters reports Japanese companies are compensating users as a wave of cyberattacks weighs on the national economy.

items.title: OpenSSL 4.1.0: What’s new, what’s removed, and what’s still broken
items.summary: OpenSSL 4.1.0 adds DTLS 1.3 support but ships with four known DTLS bugs, two of which can cause applications to misread connection state; relevant for teams adopting DTLS or the new SSL listener API.

items.title: Unpatched Tailscale SSH Flaws Could Let a Hacked Device Reach Root on Other Servers
items.summary: A researcher disclosed unpatched Tailscale SSH flaws: a compromised device with permitted access and port forwarding enabled can gain root on other reachable servers in the tailnet.

items.title: PHP2Shell Exploitation Attempts Continue Amid Suspected N. Korea Global Scanning Activity
items.summary: Unit 42 retracted its assessment that PHP2Shell flaws were exploited against a European government agency, saying the attack merely occurred in the context of a vulnerable PHP app; exploitation attempts and suspected North Korean scanning continue.

items.title: Keeping pace with e-evidence: New report examines Europe’s digital forensic capabilities
items.summary: A European Commission/Europol report finds digital forensic tools, resources and expertise across Europe are struggling to keep pace with the volume and variety of modern e-evidence.

items.title: AI slop is piling up highest on the biggest open-source projects
items.summary: A Linux Foundation survey of 234 contributors finds maintainers of large open source projects estimate nearly a third of incoming code changes are low-quality or AI-generated, driving burnout risk.

items.title: Synthetic identities leave US lenders with $2.4 billion in fraud exposure
items.summary: TransUnion reports 81% of suspected digital fraud in H1 2026 occurred at login or transaction stages, with synthetic identities leaving US lenders $2.4bn exposed.

items.title: Google open-sources the Elephant-Goldfish Model plugin its engineers use to catch AI coding mistakes
items.summary: Google open-sourced its Elephant-Goldfish Model plugin, which forces AI coding agents to write and defend a design document reviewed by independent AI sessions before code is written.

items.title: Work to protect DNS from quantum decryption attacks is speeding up
items.summary: The Register reports accelerating work to protect DNS against quantum decryption attacks, plus regional internet registry reform and scam abuse of trustworthy-sounding domains.

items.title: Anthropic's Claude accessed Georgia state vote count data behind paywall
items.summary: Reuters reports Anthropic's Claude accessed Georgia state vote count data that sat behind a paywall.

items.title: YARA-X 1.22.0 Release, (Sun, Oct 25th)
items.summary: YARA-X 1.22.0 is out with 11 improvements and 9 bug fixes, relevant for detection engineering teams.

items.title: 27 arrests and 248 potential victims identified in action week against labour exploitation
items.summary: Europol, the European Labour Authority and 34 countries report 27 arrests and 248 potential victims identified in an action week against labour exploitation in high-risk sectors.

items.title: 5th EMPACT Hackathon leads to the detection of 51 potential victims
items.summary: The fifth EMPACT Hackathon in Amsterdam brought 40 investigators from 20 countries together to target digital aspects of human trafficking, identifying 51 potential victims and five suspects.

items.title: China’s political elite gather for talks on Communist Party discipline
items.summary: China's political elite convene a four-day plenum on Communist Party discipline, watched for signals on leadership and policy direction.

items.title: Aleksandar Vucic, the Serbian leader brought down by students
items.summary: Serbian president Aleksandar Vucic concedes defeat in parliamentary elections to a student-led protest movement.

items.title: Israel’s election: Five key things to know
items.summary: Explainer on Israel's election held amid multiple wars, international criticism and domestic divisions.

items.title: It’s complicated: The status of EU-Canada relations
items.summary: Politico analysis ahead of the EU-Canada summit in Montreal, where leaders still disagree on the scope and labelling of a closer partnership, alongside Ukraine financing needs.

items.title: r/opensource bans AI projects, and solo devs go down with them
items.summary: Reddit's r/opensource has banned projects that use, are made by, or are intended for AI, adding strict age, licence and community requirements that also affect solo developers.

items.title: Putins Schattenflotte: Warum greift Deutschland nicht durch?
items.summary: German-language Politico item questioning why Germany is not acting more firmly against Russia's shadow fleet.

items.title: US military says it helped Gulf states export 1.5 billion barrels of oil
items.summary: US Central Command says it supported the transit of over 3,000 commercial vessels through the Strait of Hormuz, helping Gulf states export 1.5 billion barrels of oil.

items.title: Houthis say they attacked East-West oil pumping stations; No Saudi confirmation
items.summary: Houthis claim attacks on Saudi East-West oil pumping stations; no Saudi confirmation so far.

items.title: ISC Stormcast For Monday, October 26th, 2026 https://isc.sans.edu/podcastdetail/10150, (Mon, Oct 26th)
items.summary: SANS Internet Storm Center daily Stormcast podcast episode for 26 October 2026.

items.title: Officials from Mecca pact countries to meet Iranian officials on Monday, two sources say
items.summary: Officials from Mecca pact countries are set to meet Iranian counterparts, according to two sources.

items.title: China's Xi opens Communist Party plenum, aims for firm governance measures
items.summary: Xi Jinping opened the Communist Party plenum with a focus on firm governance measures.

items.title: Celebrations in Serbia after veteran ruler Vučić loses election to student-led protest movement
items.summary: Serbia's Vučić loses after 12 years in power to a student-led protest movement in a vote framed as a referendum on the country's direction.

items.title: Zelenskiy says US fully resumes warnings on ballistic strikes
items.summary: Zelenskiy says the US has fully resumed sharing warnings about ballistic missile strikes.

items.title: Serbia’s Vučić concedes defeat after tense parliamentary elections
items.summary: Serbia's Vučić concedes a landslide defeat to a protest-backed student movement in parliamentary elections.

items.title: France: The sickest man of Europe
items.summary: Analysis argues France, the EU's second-largest economy, is caught in a vicious cycle of fiscal and social crises.

items.title: Thousands protest Czech government's public media overhaul after rushed vote
items.summary: Thousands protest in Czechia against a rushed government overhaul of public media.

items.title: Canada and Europe want to reshape the global order. But whose vision will prevail?
items.summary: Politico examines competing Canadian and EU visions for reshaping the global order ahead of the EU-Canada summit.

items.title: Netanyahu rebuked for plan to use crypto to bypass economic sanctions
items.summary: Netanyahu faces rebuke over a plan to use cryptocurrency to bypass economic sanctions.

items.title: Former Unit 8200 Officers Raise $34 Million for Agentic SecOps Startup Mave
items.summary: Tel Aviv-based Mave, founded by Unit 8200 alumni, raised $34 million for AI agents that investigate alerts across existing security stacks.

items.title: What the US Movement Against Data Centers Can Learn From Abroad
items.summary: Wired interview with author Paris Marx on lessons the US anti-data-center movement can draw from Ireland, New Zealand and other markets.
